correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs all three OITR constraints, matches zero supports bijectively to rook matchings, and counts each weight by inclusion-exclusion with an explicitly verified neighborhood union of size s(m+n-s-1). Positive-neighbor totality is automatic except the 2x2 board, where exactly 4 weight-3 and 2 weight-4 functions require removal. Capacity-two defenders yield the optimal weight, and the exhaustive equality-case decomposition into pairings, P3-plus-pairs, or pairs-plus-singleton defenders yields the stated counts. A standalone code check implements graph neighborhoods and all original constraints and exhaustively verifies full polynomials for 2x2,2x3,2x4,2x5,3x3,3x4,3x5,4x4, using full ternary assignments or equivalently exhaustive matching supports and positive-label assignments. Finite checks complement the infinite combinatorial argument.

originality.rationale: The 2021 same-object paper provides a minimum scalar, not the cardinality polynomial or optimizer census. Direct inspection of its arXiv full text and the 2019 foundational manuscript, name/graph equivalence searches, indexed-record scientific comparisons, and comparison with accessible prior-claim corpus did not identify coverage of the whole enumerator. The value and novelty ascribed are the strictly finer polynomial and classification; the nonexceptional scalar is expressly credited as prior work. Publication-priority uncertainty remains, as documented.
residual_risks: Semantic scientific-record search and public web indexing cannot establish global nonexistence of an equivalent formula; unindexed enumerations or stronger theorems may contain it.

value.rationale: The foundational 2021 work fixes minimum weight for nearly all boards. The full rook-graph outer-independent total Roman weight polynomial is a genuinely richer two-parameter invariant giving exact counts at all redundancy levels, not a routine restatement of the scalar. Its matchings and defender-cover classification yields all optimal functions, parity-sensitive closed counts, and a mathematically necessary nontrivial low-degree exception. The calculation is motivated by enumerating robust defender deployments for a graph family singled out in the prior primary literature.
